title: SQL vs NoSQL Data Stores
intro: Choosing between Relational (SQL) and Non-Relational (NoSQL) storage engines shapes transaction semantics, query capabilities, and horizontal scaling limits.
objectives: Analyze ACID transactional guarantees vs BASE (Basically Available, Soft-state, Eventual consistency).
Classify NoSQL families: Key-Value, Document, Wide-Column, Graph, and Columnar OLAP.
Determine when to choose relational schemas vs denormalized document models.
body:
### Taxonomy of Database Engines
1. **Relational (RDBMS)**: PostgreSQL, MySQL. Rigid relational schemas, joins, B-Tree indexes, and ACID transactions. Difficult to scale writes horizontally beyond a single primary node.
2. **Key-Value**: Redis, DynamoDB. Extreme throughput ($O(1)$ lookups) by partition key. Zero relational joins.
3. **Document**: MongoDB, Couchbase. Semi-structured JSON documents. Ideal for polymorphic schemas and hierarchical data.
4. **Wide-Column (LSM)**: Apache Cassandra, ScyllaDB. Partition key + clustering column. High write throughput, scalable across global masterless clusters.
5. **Columnar OLAP**: ClickHouse, Snowflake. Organizes data by column rather than row, enabling lightning-fast analytical aggregation across billions of records.
keyIdea: Default to PostgreSQL for transactional integrity and complex relational queries. Adopt NoSQL when write volume, global replication, or specific data shapes (graphs, timeseries) exceed RDBMS limits.

concepts.title: B-Tree vs LSM-Tree
concepts.body: B-Trees optimize for random reads with in-place page updates ($O(\log N)$). LSM-Trees optimize for write throughput with sequential appends and background compaction.

concepts.title: Denormalization
concepts.body: Duplicating data across documents to eliminate expensive cross-node joins at query time.

examples: Stripe using PostgreSQL for transaction ledgers; Uber using Cassandra for driver location histories.

quiz.prompt: Which database engine family is best optimized for high-volume analytical aggregations (e.g. SUM, AVG) across billions of historical records?
quiz.explanation: Columnar storage reads only the relevant columns from disk into memory, delivering orders of magnitude faster analytics.
